top.title: 2027: Malami condemns alleged attacks on ADC campaign
top.description: Former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, has condemned alleged attacks and acts of intimidation against members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. Malami, the ADC governorship candidate in Kebbi State, also expressed appreciation to residents for what he described as the massive turnout and support for former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the party’s leadership at the campaign event held on Thursday, November 5. In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Assistant on Media, Mohammed Bello Doka, Malami said the turnout demonstrated the people’s determination to pursue a better future for the state and the country. He commended Atiku for his leadership and commitment to national renewal, while acknowledging the contributions of the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, other party leaders, campaign coordinators, supporters and volunteers. Malami said the party was committed to building a Nigeria that was affordable and secure, identifying rising fuel costs, insecurity and unemployment as issues requiring urgent attention. He also outlined his priorities for Kebbi to include agricultural transformation, quality education, accessible healthcare, youth empowerment, security, local government autonomy and accountable governance. However, he expressed concern over reports of attacks on members of the campaign convoy, destruction of media equipment and the alleged use of tear gas around areas occupied by members of the visiting delegation. He said any involvement of government institutions or security agencies in such incidents would be unacceptable and called for an investigation. Malami also condemned the demolition of the Malami Pressure Group (MPG) headquarters along Sani Abacha Bypass, Birnin Kebbi, describing the circumstances surrounding the incident as troubling. He said the Kebbi State Government’s denial of involvement and its attribution of the demolition to a private ownership dispute did not remove the need for transparency and accountability. According to him, political disagreements should not be used to justify intimidation, destruction of property or the suppression of lawful opposition. Malami said the constitutional rights to freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly must be respected by all levels of government. On the challenges facing Kebbi, he listed banditry, displacement, poverty, food insecurity and disruption of agricultural activities, citing the National Emergency Management Agency’s humanitarian intervention in March 2026 for victims of banditry in Shanga, Yauri and Bunza. top.title: Pope says in ‘fairly good shape’ after lung cancer surgery
top.description: Pope Leo XIV said Friday he was in “fairly good shape” after lung cancer surgery last month as he began a 12-day tour of South America with a visit to Uruguay. “I know some people were doubtful about this trip taking place,” Leo told reporters on board the papal plane. “I had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward. And I am very happy to say praise the Lord and thanks to wonderful medical assistance, I’m here today, I think in fairly good shape,” he said. Leo, 71, had a cancerous tumor and part of his right lung removed in an operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital on October 13. He was discharged on October 17 and doctors quoted by the Vatican have said he is fit to travel and does not require any further therapy. Asked by reporters if he had advice for people facing a cancer diagnosis, he said: “Not to be afraid. “Early detection is obviously the best way to go and so regular check-ups are a blessing. And take care of yourselves,” he said. Leo was also asked if he had resumed playing tennis — a favorite sport. “Not yet, but I will,” he said. top.title: 2027: Atiku’s aide tackles Keyamo over exclusion from ballot
top.description: An aide to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has criticised the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, over his remarks that the heavens would not fall if Atiku was excluded from the 2027 presidential ballot. Ibe, who described Keyamo’s position as an attempt to undermine Nigerians’ democratic rights, said excluding a major political challenger would erode public confidence in the electoral process. He stated this in a Facebook post while reacting to Keyamo’s comments on the possibility of Atiku not participating in the 2027 presidential election. Ibe argued that the exclusion of a major challenger should not be treated as inconsequential, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to decide their preferred presidential candidate through the ballot. “When a ruling party treats the exclusion of a major challenger as inconsequential, it is asking Nigerians to accept that their choice is inconsequential too. That is how you erode public faith in democracy,” he said. Challenging Keyamo, Ibe asked why the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would welcome the prospect of an election without Atiku if it was confident in President Bola Tinubu’s performance. He insisted that Tinubu should be allowed to defend his record before Nigerians, while Atiku should also be given the opportunity to present his case to the electorate. Ibe expressed confidence that Atiku would secure widespread support in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, saying the former vice president’s supporters were prepared to translate their support into votes. “On 16 January 2027, we intend to turn the support Nigerians have shown Atiku into votes and those votes into a mandate. If Nigerians send Tinubu packing at the ballot box, it will be political hell for an APC that has grown accustomed to taking them for granted,” he said. The former vice president’s aide also invoked an Igbo proverb to caution Keyamo and the APC against disregarding the wishes of voters. He quoted the saying, “A gwa ntị okwu, ntị anụghị, e gburu isi, e gburu ya na ntị,” which he translated to mean that when the ear refuses to heed counsel, it shares the fate of the head when it is lost. According to him, a political party that refuses to listen to voters should be prepared for their response on election day. Ibe further vowed that Atiku’s supporters would defend their right to choose their preferred candidate through all lawful means and exercise that right at the polls. He, however, ended his post with a sharp personal attack on Keyamo, saying the minister and his supporters belonged in hell. top.description: The management of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) on Friday said grid instability was not responsible for the Ikeja Electric (IE) Band A outage reported by the company on Nov. 3 and Nov. 4. Ms. Ndidi Mba, the General Manager of the Corporate Communication Unit of TCN, disclosed this in a statement in Lagos. According to her, TCN described the attribution as inaccurate and misleading, saying that the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid was not the responsibility of a Distribution Company (DisCo). “By virtue of Section 67 of the Electricity Act 2023, the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid falls exclusively within the defined functions of the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO). “IE, like every other market participant, has no authority to make such determinations, and NISO has made no such attribution of the outages in IE’s notice to TCN,” she said. Mba said that NISO had already explained the situation, attributing the current decline in power generation to gas supply constraints to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower reservoir inflows. She said that the reduced generation had affected the energy allocated to DisCos, resulting in fewer hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. “The impact on each DisCo varies with available generation and its allocation,” she said. Mba said that the shortfall in electricity supply to IE’s customers was a consequence of reduced generation and the resulting allocation, not any failure of TCN’s transmission network. “TCN can only transmit the energy made available to it and cannot transmit energy that is not generated. “The records for all feeders supplying IE confirm the national picture NISO described. “Of the interruptions recorded on Nov. 1 and 2, 68 percent were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation. “A further 26 percent were due to IE’s non-compliance with load allocation by the National Control Centre (NCC) of NISO or to faults and works on IKEDC’s own network. “The remaining six percent were TCN planned maintenance, switching, or a line limitation. top.description: Detroit Tigers outfielder Max Clark described the kind of player he is in a clip MLB Network posted, and he put the grit first. “I feel like I have that gritty – there’s some flash in there, but I play hard and I’ll run in your face, I’ll throw you out, I’ll hit a homer and play defense,” Clark said in the clip, which Tigers On SI transcribed . Clark was describing Detroit when he got to that line. “It’s a city where everyone works hard, grinds and wants to come together as one big city. I feel like I have that in my game,” he said. “It’s a little bit of everything, but it’s all based on hard work and determination to be better than you and I think that’s what the backbone of that city is built off of.” "It's a city where everyone works hard, grinds and wants to come together as one big city. I feel like I have that in my game…" @maxxclarkk13 shares why his play style is a fit in Detroit 🐯 pic.twitter.com/bfWVaZuTnC — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 3, 2026 Detroit Tigers center fielder Max Clark (15) bats against Pittsburgh Pirates during the fifth inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Max Clark Had a Solid 2026 Season for the Detroit Tigers Clark played 51 games for Detroit in 2026 after making his debut on July 31 against the Athletics , a 13-1 win in which he went 3-for-4 with two doubles. He hit .272 with three home runs and 23 RBIs, and he stole five bases on six attempts. Clark finished with a .350 on-base percentage, a .417 slugging percentage and a .766 OPS. He is 21 years old. Clark Needs to Be an Everyday Outfielder in 2027 When opening day 2027 arrives for Detroit, Clark has to be one of the three starting outfielders. Riley Greene will be another starter in the outfield. With questions about Kerry Carpenter and Parker Meadows, Clark is clearly better than those two players. The Tigers want their young players to contribute. Center field is the opening. Meadows started 11 of the Tigers’ first 13 games there in 2026 before an April 9 collision with Greene sent him to the hospital, and Clark is the center fielder on Detroit’s depth chart now. Prospect Zyhir Hope , who came to Detroit from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, is another player who could crack the Tigers outfield at some point in 2027. However, Clark and Kevin McGonigle are two young players in Detroit who play with swagger, and both are cornerstone pieces for the long haul.

But the front office is still facing a lot of huge calls in any deal involving Porzingis. And according to Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints , the Warriors have contacted the Milwaukee Bucks , Chicago Bulls , and New Orleans Pelicans about a deal involving Porzingis. top.title: ‘Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years,’: Knicks set the record straight after players named her ‘fakest celebrity fan’
top.description: Jun 10, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Taylor Swift reacts after the New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in game four of the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Taylor Swift caught some unexpected shade from a pair of New York Knicks players this week, who named her the team’s fakest celebrity fan. But it turns out that the Knicks organization doesn’t see it that way. On Friday, the Knicks released a statement backing Swift, making it clear that they appreciate her support. The statement came less than a day after Tyler Kolek and Miles “Deuce” McBride questioned her fandom during a livestream. ‘Fakest celebrity fan’ Kolek and McBride were playing NBA 2K during a TikTok livestream on Thursday when they were asked to name the fakest celebrity Knicks fan. Kolek floated Swift’s name , though he acknowledged that her busy schedule might keep her from attending more games. “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek said. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride agreed with his teammate’s pick. “I would agree,” McBride said. “Swifties not gonna like that answer.” The pair also suggested that Swift’s appearances at Madison Square Garden were “a little performative.” Instead, they gave their seal of approval to regulars like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan, who they approved of as real fans of the team. It wasn’t the first time that Swift’s Knicks fandom has been questioned. During the NBA Finals, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy said he was “sick of her” after she attended games. Knicks Respond The Knicks didn’t waste much time responding. Hours after the livestream, the team reached out to TMZ Sports with a statement. “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the Knicks said, via TMZ . Swift’s history with the Knicks goes back more than two decades. According to TMZ, she sang at the Garden as part of a Knicks halftime kids’ talent contest in 2003, when she was 13, and she has said that’s when she became a fan. She was also courtside for the Knicks’ historic Game 4 comeback in the NBA Finals in June, on the way to the franchise’s first championship in 53 years. And of course, she and Travis Kelce got married at Madison Square Garden in July. Needless to say, it’s going to be hard to convince the Knicks that Swift isn’t a real fan. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases have been reported across the country of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year in the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. nigeria.title: I’ll sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight – Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Nwafor Sunday President Bola Tinubu has said he will spend the night in Akwa Ibom State, declaring that his visit is a “second term presidential sleep” as he expressed confidence in securing re-election in 2027. Tinubu made the remark on Friday during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. Addressing the crowd, the President thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 general election. “Thank you, Akwa Ibom. I love you with my heart. I will sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight. It’s going to be a second term presidential sleep. I will dream of victory too. “I will depend on you to go out and vote. The weapon you have is the PVC. If you have not collected it, please go ahead and collect your PVC. I am begging you, for the sake of your future,” he said. Tinubu also reiterated his administration’s promises of improved living conditions, infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and job creation. “I promised you a better future, I promised you development, I promised you education. I promised you skill development, I promised you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees,” he added. The President’s declaration comes amid criticism from the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, who had taken a swipe at him over his travels across the country. Obi had suggested that Tinubu had not spent the night in any state outside Abuja and Lagos, a remark that appeared to question the President’s physical presence across the country. Tinubu’s announcement that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom comes against the backdrop of the exchange between the two political figures as political activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather momentum. nigeria.title: Tinubu Approves Ibom Deep-Sea Port, Akwa Ibom International Airport Status
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the proposed Ibom Deep-Sea Port and the upgrade of the Victor Attah International Airport in Akwa Ibom State to international airport status. The President announced the approvals while addressing residents of the state at a rally held in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday He had made a similar promise during his 2023 presidential campaign rally at the same stadium, pledging to establish a deep-sea port in Akwa Ibom. He cited the Lekki Deep Sea Port, developed during his tenure as Lagos State Governor, as a model for the proposed project. Tinubu urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the electoral process. “I heard from my friend, my governor, my pastor, on behalf of the people and leadership of Akwa Ibom, a request for Ibom’s deep-sea port. Ibom Deep-Sea Port. It’s approved,” Tinubu said. The approval came after Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, pledged that the state would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 if the Federal Government approved and facilitated the delivery of the Ibom Deep-Sea Port project. ﻿ “Give us Ibom Deep Seaport, we will deliver two million votes. This deep seaport is capable of unlocking the economy of the state, the South-South region and Nigeria at large,” Eno said. On infrastructure, the President disclosed that he had approved the request by the state leadership for the Victor Attah International Airport to attain international airport status. He promised a better future for the people of Akwa Ibom, pledging investments in education, skills development, job creation and economic growth. He said his administration would support the development of economic opportunities in the state, particularly through the cultivation and processing of palm produce. “There is no reason why Akwa Ibom cannot use the value of palm trees and the palms here. There is no reason that we cannot create skills, developmental skills, that are enduring and everlasting,” he said. The President said the port would generate economic value and promote development in the state. He stressed that development must be inclusive and capable of creating tangible economic benefits for the people. Tinubu also urged residents to support the state governor, encouraging them to follow his leadership and heed his guidance. nigeria.title: Lagos seals over 45 buildings in Eko, Ifako-Ijaiye
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Physical Planning Permit Authority (LASPPPA) has sealed more than 45 buildings in Eko and Ifako-Ijaiye districts over alleged violations of physical planning regulations. The enforcement exercises were carried out by the authority’s Monitoring and Compliance Unit on Wednesday in Ifako-Ijaiye District and Thursday in Eko District. In a statement shared on its Facebook page on Thursday, LASPPPA said 25 properties were sealed in Ifako-Ijaiye for operating without valid planning permits, excessive density, illegal remodelling, deviation from approved plans and ongoing construction without approval. In a separate update on Friday, the agency disclosed that more than 20 buildings were sealed in Eko District for various planning violations. It said 10 properties were found to have deviated from their approved building plans, while five were sealed for excessive density and another five for carrying out remodelling without the required permits. Other affected properties were sealed for undertaking construction work without planning approval. According to LASPPPA, the affected property owners and developers had earlier been served contravention notices by the respective district offices but failed to comply with the directives. “Contravention notices had been served by the district office previously, but compliance was not achieved,” the agency stated. The authority advised owners and developers of the affected properties to visit their nearest LASPPPA district office or its headquarters at Oba Akinjobi Way, GRA, Ikeja, for regularisation and further guidance. Meanwhile, a source in the agency, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said monitoring and enforcement of physical planning regulations were continuous exercises. nigeria.title: Just in: Tinubu approves Ibom Deep Seaport in Akwa Ibom
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the long-awaited Ibom Deep Seaport project in Akwa Ibom State following a request by Governor Umo Eno. Tinubu announced the approval on Friday while responding to the governor’s appeal during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. The President, who was in the state to inaugurate projects executed by the Eno administration, said development must promote inclusive growth, create economic value and improve the lives of the people. Responding to Eno’s request for the deep seaport, Tinubu said: “Now, development must be even inclusive and reasonable, must bring progress and create economic value. I heard from my friend, my governor, my pastor, on behalf of the people and leadership of Akwa Ibom, request for Ibom’s deep-sea port.” After repeating the request, the President asked the crowd, “Will you vote?” He subsequently declared, “Okay, it’s approved.” The approval followed a pledge by Eno that Akwa Ibom would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 if the Federal Government approved and delivered the seaport project. “Give us Ibom Deep Seaport, we will deliver two million votes. This deep seaport is capable of unlocking the economy of the state, the South-South region and Nigeria at large,” the governor said. Eno described the project as the most important economic demand of the people of Akwa Ibom, saying it would transform the state’s maritime, industrial and employment sectors. He said the people had remained loyal to Tinubu since 2023 and were asking him to fulfil his earlier promise to establish the facility. Tinubu had, during his 2023 presidential campaign rally at the same stadium, promised to build the deep seaport, citing the Lekki Deep Seaport, developed during his tenure as Lagos State governor, as an example of what he intended to achieve in Akwa Ibom. Eno recalled that the project, originally conceived during the administration of former Governor Victor Attah as the Ibaka Deep Seaport and Industrial City, had remained unrealised for decades despite featuring in successive presidential campaigns. “This seaport would serve as a major transhipment hub. It will create thousands of jobs for our people. It will open Akwa Ibom to international trade and investment,” he said. The governor also said Akwa Ibom had aligned with the Federal Government by joining the All Progressives Congress (APC) to attract greater federal presence and development to the state. He assured Tinubu of the state’s support for his re-election bid in 2027, describing the proposed seaport as a major development expected from the President’s administration. nigeria.title: Kenyan preacher sentenced to 200 years in prison over child murders
nigeria.description: A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for the murder of 190 children and one adult in an infamous starvation cult. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the sect’s base near the coastal resort of Malindi, in what became known as the “Shakahola Forest Massacre”. Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, was accused of inciting his followers to starve themselves to death to “meet Jesus”. He was convicted last month of murdering 191 people between January 2021 and September 2023, alongside 28 co-accused. On Friday, the court sentenced him to 100 years for the homicide charges and 100 years for the starvation charges, while his accomplices — many of whom starved their own children to death — received a variety of lengthy prison terms. “Children observed siblings drop dead… as their parents ate and drank,” the judge said. “Some died as a result of strangulation, severely beaten… Children were subjected to extreme suffering… terrifying living conditions, psychological trauma.” Mackenzie was impassive as the sentence was read out, as he had been throughout the trial. Prosecutors had called for the death penalty, but the judge said it would “fail to achieve deterrence, particularly where the convicts regard death as a pathway to heaven and a union with Jesus and their deceased children.” Kenya has the death penalty but has not carried out an execution since 1987. Francis Wanje, a 62-year-old teacher who lost two grandchildren to the cult, told AFP he had hoped Mackenzie would be sentenced to death to prevent further tragedies. Another of his grandchildren, now 11, went without food for eight days before being rescued in March 2023. He testified that his brothers, aged two and five, had died after their parents, acting on the guru’s orders, forbade them from eating or drinking. “Nothing can ease the pain,” said Wanje, who blamed authorities for failing to act swiftly. “I really have great (anger) towards the authorities. If they had taken action, we would not be here today,” he added. – Death penalty – Mackenzie’s lawyer said he would appeal the verdict. He also faces manslaughter and terrorism charges in other trials, which he denies. Around 120 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial. According to witnesses, the movement denounced formal education as “satanic”, viewed modern medicine and hospitals as instruments of the devil and required followers to cut themselves off from the outside world. Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 after a rights group alerted authorities and some followers were rescued from the 325-hectare (800-acre) ranch in the Shakahola forest on Kenya’s coast. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . business.title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. In a post on X that led with the outperformance figure, Strive also highlighted a year-to-date bitcoin yield of 63.2% and a bitcoin dollar gain of $9.00 per assumed diluted share outstanding, both measured through Sept. 30. Strive acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter at an average cost of about $78,885 and 20,373 bitcoin over the nine months ended Sept. 30. business.title: Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported , a procedural step that usually precedes public release. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion. The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. It lowers the litigation risk for employers that decide they want to. JUST IN: The White House is now reviewing a new rule which will allow Americans to invest in crypto through their 401(k) retirement plans pic.twitter.com/uXGGIXEzdC — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What the DOL safe harbor covers President Donald Trump’s Aug. 7, 2025, executive order, “Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors,” directed the Labor secretary to reexamine ERISA guidance and, where appropriate, propose rules with “appropriately calibrated safe harbors.” The order defined alternative assets to include private-market equity and debt, real estate, holdings in actively managed vehicles that invest in digital assets, commodities, infrastructure and lifetime-income strategies. The March proposal implements that order. A DOL fact sheet said prudence under ERISA is process-based and that fiduciaries retain discretion to select any designated investment alternative if they follow the outlined review. Deputy Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling cast the approach as neutral: “The department’s days of picking winners and losers are over.” That stance reverses a prior chill. In May 2025 the DOL rescinded its March 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use “extreme care” before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu. The department said that phrase was not found in ERISA and restored a context-specific standard. Later, it was reported that Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren pressed the DOL to abandon the crypto-friendly path. House Republicans have separately pushed to codify Trump’s crypto order in statute. business.title: Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain. Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. How the XRP started moving The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers. The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far. Why XRP and bitcoin matter here Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses. All of the stolen SOL, about $87 million at Elliptic’s prices, has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, with much of it ending as bitcoin. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year, both ahead of estimates, CNBC reported . Prior months were revised higher as well. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported. The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Spot bitcoin changed hands around $75,800 after the data, with a market cap of about $1.52 trillion and roughly $48 billion in trading volume over the past day, Yahoo Finance data indicated. Bitcoin price reaction Bitcoin price’s first move was a quick spike above $76,100, then a slide toward $75,600 before it settled back near $75,800. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced. That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. Most of the damage to the bitcoin price this week came from equity risk-off, not from the labor market itself, and a hot payrolls number mainly reinforces the path the Fed was already pricing. CME FedWatch odds put roughly a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting after the release, up from about 70% into the open. The next employment report is due Dec. 4, five days before that decision, and the signal points the same way the last Fed hold did: stronger hiring and firmer wages leave less room for another pause. Tech rout aftermath and ETF outflows Thursday’s session still sets the floor under the bitcoin price. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below its recent high, while the S&P 500 lost about 4.4% and the Dow shed roughly 1,800 points, or 3.4%, CNBC reported . The Magnificent Seven erased more than $1 trillion in market value. Nvidia alone lost more than 9%, wiping out roughly $440 billion in capitalization, as investors priced in a slower AI data-center buildout after the Democratic midterm sweep. Bitcoin has traded with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year, so a correction in the Nasdaq has pulled the bitcoin price lower even when on-chain flows looked steady. business.title: South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended withdrawals and trading on Friday after receiving a hacking-threat email, and said it is moving all held virtual assets into offline cold wallets as a preemptive step to protect customer funds. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. The company has not set a date to reopen trading or standard withdrawals. What Gopax closed and what still works With trading offline, all open orders were canceled, Chosun Biz reported . Deposits were initially paused with withdrawals; later Korean coverage said deposits had been restored while web and app withdrawals stayed shut. Manual withdrawals through support will take longer than usual. A cold wallet is a storage setup kept offline, cut off from the internet that hot wallets use to process customer sends. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . A rough stretch for Korean crypto platforms The freeze lands in a week when exchange security is already under a bright light. On Oct. 29, attackers drained about $6.34 billion from Binance hot wallets in what Binance later described as a months-long campaign that began with a fake job interview. The FBI has tied that theft to North Korea; Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it is covering customer losses from its own funds. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals earlier this week after its own security incident, with preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers near $40 million. Gopax’s case is different on the facts disclosed so far: the exchange is describing a threat email and a precautionary lockdown, not a confirmed drain. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. This emotional homecoming adds weight to a game where the Wizards must fix their defense. The Hawks made 19 three-pointers in the first matchup while Washington only made six. Atlanta now averages about 15 made threes per game compared to the Wizards’ nine. The Wizards need to stop leaking out on defense and box out better to win Friday. Trae Young’s Homecoming and the Revenge Narrative Trae Young spent seven seasons in Atlanta before joining the Wizards. His return to State Farm Arena marks a rare moment for a player facing his former team. Yahoo Sports reports that this marks the first occasion Young has come back to Atlanta representing the opposing team. He holds the top spots in the record books for assists and three-pointers. sports.title: ‘Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years,’: Knicks set the record straight after players named her ‘fakest celebrity fan’
sports.description: Jun 10, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Taylor Swift reacts after the New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in game four of the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Taylor Swift caught some unexpected shade from a pair of New York Knicks players this week, who named her the team’s fakest celebrity fan. But it turns out that the Knicks organization doesn’t see it that way. On Friday, the Knicks released a statement backing Swift, making it clear that they appreciate her support. The statement came less than a day after Tyler Kolek and Miles “Deuce” McBride questioned her fandom during a livestream. ‘Fakest celebrity fan’ Kolek and McBride were playing NBA 2K during a TikTok livestream on Thursday when they were asked to name the fakest celebrity Knicks fan. Kolek floated Swift’s name , though he acknowledged that her busy schedule might keep her from attending more games. “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek said. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride agreed with his teammate’s pick. “I would agree,” McBride said. “Swifties not gonna like that answer.” The pair also suggested that Swift’s appearances at Madison Square Garden were “a little performative.” Instead, they gave their seal of approval to regulars like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan, who they approved of as real fans of the team. It wasn’t the first time that Swift’s Knicks fandom has been questioned. During the NBA Finals, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy said he was “sick of her” after she attended games. Swift’s history with the Knicks goes back more than two decades. sports.title: Preseason Thunder will not return to Daytona in 2027
sports.description: Motorsport photo Fans have been calling for the return of Preseason Thunder at Daytona International Speedway, which served as a pre-season test and the first glimpse of new driver/team combinations. In April, NASCAR's John Probst indicated that a January test at Daytona was likely to return, but plans have since changed. The original plan was to use the test to improve the superspeedway package, but NASCAR now appears more satisfied with the current package after recent changes to the spoiler and horsepower over the summer. NASCAR still sees areas to address, especially in regards to extreme fuel-saving, which has become a major feature of the opening stages at superspeedway races. However, NASCAR CEO Steve O'Donnell said NASCAR currently has no plans to hold the test . General view General view “On our end, you look at the changes we’ve made, and this goes back to our competition group, we’ve said we’re going to move fast," said O'Donnell. "I think historically at NASCAR we would have said, we’ll see in 2027 and we’ll talk about the short track package in 2028. That’s not the case. We moved quickly. From an on-track competition car, are you able to move and do some different things directionally? I think we’re comfortable with heading to Daytona with what we saw. "Now, kind of the officiating or sporting regulations, I think we are taking a look at. With technology, with AI, it's become such a focus on fuel-saving. If you ask the drivers if they ever fuel saved at Talladega ten years ago, the answer is yes. That's always happened. But it's become such a focus now on what you can do and the strategy in the race. "That is the focus in terms of how does the actual race play out, not necessarily the car, but what does the race look like in terms of is it stages or whatever we may do during the race. "But we don't have plans right now to go test at Daytona." sports.title: Browns Coach Sends Strong Message About Shedeur Sanders
sports.description: The Cleveland Browns are set to get their first look at Shedeur Sanders in his second season on Sunday afternoon against the New Orleans Saints on the road. Deshaun Watson is set to miss this week’s game due to a concussion. That has given Sanders a chance to get on the field and show what he’s capable of producing after a full offseason of development. Sanders showed some signs of starting potential during his rookie season. He also had his fair share of bad moments. When all was said and done in 2025, Sanders played in eight games and completed 56.6 percent of his pass attempts for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. Sanders also ran for 169 yards and a touchdown. This week, he’ll attempt to show enough to force head coach Todd Monken to keep him on the field moving forward. Speaking of Monken, the head coach spoke out about Sanders taking the field this week. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Browns’ Todd Monken Sends Honest Message About Shedeur Sanders As shared by ESPN’s Daniel Oyefus, Monken made it clear that he is excited to see Sanders on the field this week. “I’m fired up to see him play,” Monken said . “I mean, who wouldn’t be?” If things go well for Sanders this week, he could force Monken to make a difficult decision. At 24 years old, the former Colorado standout is still capable of being a long-term option for the Browns. Cleveland needs to find out what it truly has in Sanders before the end of the season. On the flip side, if things go poorly, the Browns will easily be able to shift back to Watson for the next game. Since being drafted, Sanders has become one of the most talked about players in the NFL. He has also been included in trade rumors leading up to the Tuesday deadline. A strong performance could help Cleveland move him if the franchise chooses to do so. Only time will tell what the future has in store for the son of the legendary Deion Sanders. Kickoff on Sunday is scheduled for 1:00 p.m ET against the Saints. Sanders will look to prove that he deserves to have a long future with the Browns. technology.title: The folks behind John Wick are back with Karōshi trailer
technology.description: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called Karōshi (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027. Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden, where some 700 workers die each year from overwork. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( karōjisatsu in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface. Teo Yoo ( Past Lives ) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun , as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu. technology.title: Wisconsin reports measles death of a baby, first death in over 35 years
technology.description: An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the first measles death in the state since 1990, officials reported Thursday . The death comes amid an outbreak in the Badger State that has stricken over 430 people across 13 counties this year. "Any death of a child is a tragedy, and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease," Wisconsin Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. "Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family." The baby's death is the third measles fatality nationally just this week, following the death of a New York child reported on Monday and another death in Pennsylvania reported on Wednesday . The Pennsylvania death was of an unvaccinated person in Jefferson County; the state health department did not provide additional details, such as the age of the person. technology.title: Mac lookalikes multiply as Linux raids Apple's wardrobe
technology.description: Linux can do many things, but good looks aren't always its strong point. Apple has rather more of a reputation in that department, and a crop of new projects is bringing Mac-style polish to the open source desktop. Some are all-new, such as the Argentinian Lord OS , a whole new GUI desktop on top of Debian. Another, Cutefish , is a revival of a pre-ChatGPT project that never got as far as a complete release. Now it has version 1.0 for both x86-64 and Arm64, plus it's working on Mac binary compatibility via a work-in-progress layer called Reef . Ukrainian Desert OS is already at version 5.5 – practically a venerable elder in this company, despite appearing to be only about a year old. Meanwhile, ClokeOS uses Xfce for its desktop, but underneath, the OS is based on Apple's FOSS XNU kernel. The project lead plans to offer compatibility with multiple types of binaries: Linux apps, plus Mac apps via Darling , and Windows apps via Wine. This isn't new. Much as Cutefish has been revived, last year we reported on PearOS Linux , a very Mac-like skin on KDE Plasma. It has hooks in place for ambitious future features, such as Siri-style speech recognition. What's striking is the number of projects appearing and the pace of their development. Some offer both x86-64 and Arm64 builds, with Raspberry Pi editions in certain cases. For human coders, this would be months of hard work, but if it's just checking an additional box in an LLM development tool, then why wouldn't you? It's almost no extra work, but it widens the potential audience. Coveting Mac-like good looks is a longstanding urge among Linux users, and with legitimate reason. There's nothing wrong with Macs, even if you are mainly a FOSS user. Modern macOS, or OS X as it was called a decade ago, is a Unix underneath its shiny proprietary desktop, and many of the flagship Linux FOSS apps also have Mac versions, from Firefox and Thunderbird, via LibreOffice, to VirtualBox, plus less well-known but very handy apps such as Ferdium and Panwriter. We've written about the usefulness of FOSS apps on macOS before, including for reviving elderly Macs . Just a couple of months ago, we published a two-part guide on how to give Xfce a macOS-like layout and then how to tweak it so apps fit in better . We focused on the functionality, though, not the looks – we don't really care much for such things. If it does matter to you, though, you're not alone, and there are lots of themes and skins to make Xfce look prettier. Some of these are all-in-one packages that you can install on an existing distro to give it a new look. One recent example is Cupertino , developed with assistance from Claude. From a few years ago, there are Small Sur and Ventura-Xfce . From nine years ago, long pre-LLM, there is osXFCE . We can see the appeal. technology.title: Oak Ridge labs gets hybrid quantum-HPC system to test qubit error correction
technology.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) now boasts a system for research into quantum error correction, combining IBM quantum processors with a high-performance compute (HPC) system based on AMD silicon. The Quantum Science Center ( QSC ) at ORNL, funded by the US Department of Energy (DoE), unveiled what it calls a co-design platform for quantum error correction, marrying up quantum and HPC technology. While useful, fault-tolerant quantum systems always seem to be at least a decade away, there have been notable advances over the past several years in the field of quantum error correction, according to ORNL. These include early demonstrations of protecting quantum information from environmental noise, which can cause loss of the fragile quantum states needed for computations. "Solving the challenges of quantum error correction is essential to making quantum computing a practical tool for scientific discovery, which is a priority for Oak Ridge National Laboratory," said QSC director Travis Humble. IBM Fellow and director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta said that it was no longer a question of whether error correction works, but how to accelerate and optimize error correction to build systems that scientists can use to tackle challenging problems. "This new co-design platform for quantum error correction allows us to evaluate different approaches and determine the architectures, software and workflows that will scale," he stated. ORNL's new tool combines an IBM Quantum System Two, equipped with the latest 120-qubit Nighthawk r2 quantum processors , and Umbra, a classical HPC system powered by AMD 5th Gen Epyc CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators. According to AMD, the CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate everything, while the GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads. Also part of the system are AMD Versal SoCs to provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities for the quantum circuitry. ORNL says that this brings together the computing infrastructure needed for quantum error correction in a single environment, and opens it up to more researchers than ever before. They will use it to develop and validate quantum algorithms, workflows, and applications in an environment built for quantum-centric supercomputing, an emerging paradigm where quantum processors (QPUs), CPUs, and GPUs work together as one system. IBM says that one promising approach the co-design platform cloud explore is hierarchical error correction. It describes this as using an inner code to protect qubits within a module, while an outer code wraps around the inner code’s logical qubits and adds a second layer of protection. This approach could reach a trillion logical operations at a physical error rate of one in a thousand, IBM research suggested. technology.title: RIP to the world’s ugliest car
technology.description: Elon Musk has hit the brakes on the Cybertruck, announcing on X that Tesla will wind down production at its Texas factory around mid-2027. Despite years of delays , the stainless-steel turd Musk claimed was a futuristic, apocalypse-proof tank straight out of Blade Runner is headed for a production wind-down after roughly four years, putting the Cybertruck alongside such automotive flops as the Edsel and the DeLorean. We can’t even put the Cybertruck on the same tier as the Ford Pinto, as that deathtrap was produced for a decade. The first Cybertruck lumbered off Tesla’s production line in mid-2023 before going on sale later that year , and it was practically right out of the gate that the problems began. Within months of the first deliveries, recall notices began piling up on the monstrosity. Trim pieces were flying off, internal components were failing, cameras were malfunctioning – all in all, the thing has faced 11 recalls since hitting the road in late 2023, most recently in April 2026, when a defect in brake rotors was found to potentially cause cracks that could allow wheel studs to separate from their hubs. Musk had pinned a lot of Tesla's hopes on the Cybertruck a few years ago, describing it during the company's Q3 2023 earnings call as "a great product" that would eventually generate "significant positive cash flow" for Tesla. Musk said on that same earnings call that Tesla intended to ramp Cybertruck production up to 250,000 vehicles per year by 2025 to meet the over one million Cybertruck reservations he claimed Tesla had taken. science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere.
